title: What a Chautauqua was
summary: Howard explains Chautauqua pieces as slow, technical classical cornet music requiring reading, and he cannot recall the tune.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Would you -- are you ready? Paul?
Huh?
Would you mind explaining what a Chattagua is?
A Chattagua?
Yes. Can you move closer to the mike there?
A Chattagua is nothing but a -- where you would sit down and play somewhere, and you have -- play a band -- a band number or something, and go sit down, that's all.
Well, isn't it a certain type of music?
No, just anything. Anything.
What's that?
Anything that you could play. They never bothered you about playing the Chattagua
Well, would somebody ask you to play a Chattagua? Is that the certain type of --
Yes, uh-huh.
Well, what would it be, what kind of rhythm, something fast, something slow?
Something slow.
Slow? A slow piece would be a Chattagua?
Yes.
What would the rhythm be, as far as the time signature? Would it be like 4/4, 6/8, 2/4?
What's it be? Oh, boy -- 2/4 or 6/8 or something like that, you know.
Uh-huh.
It wouldn't be fast or nothing. Just (inaudible), straightly on.
Would the Chautauqua be played in a lot of jazz clubs or would it be played more where there would be dancing?
It would be more where the people would have -- I was going to school then.
Uh-huh.

And when I finished with school that was one of my chronic pieces I had to play, and I can't remember what it was, because they'd ask me, tell me a half a dozen times to play it over again, but I didn't remember. I can't remember it now. It's just gone away from me.
Was it difficult music to play? Was it technically --
Yeah, it was kind of technical.
Sort of fast, quick, you had to have technique to master it, or could anyone play a Chautauqua?
Anyone could play a Chautauqua if they
had any kind of musical education.
Yeah, but I mean you needed some technical background, didn't you? Sounds like it was not just a very easy piece to play?
Sounded like what?
It sounded like it wasn't an easy piece, or was it very simple to play or did you have to have good technique?
You had to have good technique. You had to be able to play.
You had to be able to read, or could you use the play it by ear?
You had to be able to read the music.
You had to read it. Could you put the ear on it? Did a lot of musicians who --
No.
-- couldn't read, could they play it?
Yeah, if they could read. If they could read.
If they could read they could play it, but could they put their ear on it and learn it?
No, no.
Okay. That gives me an idea.
No, uh-uh, they can't do that.
Now, you were playing that mainly on
* A chautauqua is not a musical type or style but an educational assemblage where participants present their special skills.
I was playing it on cornet. That thing was (inaudible) you get me tied up so I can't get out. Let me get out of here.
You're out. You got out that time.
(Inaudible) on cornet?
So would it be something -- When we're talking about cornet, would it be, you know, I keep thinking of something that would be triple tonguing.
It might have been, I don't know.
Rather than legato, you know, a lot of difficult tonguing passages.

Well, the only thing about it was I got the -- I had the piece and I can't remember the tune I was playing. If I could remember the tune I could play it, I could tell you what the time was and everything.
Uh-huh.
But I can't remember.
